entries: The peregrine falcon is the fastest animal, diving at over 300 km/h. The cheetah is the fastest land animal (about 100–120 km/h in short bursts), and the sailfish is among the fastest fish.
Some animals live extremely long: the Greenland shark can live around 400 years, giant tortoises over 150 years, and the bowhead whale over 200 years. Some sponges and jellyfish live even longer.
A mammal is a warm-blooded animal with hair or fur that feeds its young with milk, like humans, dogs, whales and bats. Most give birth to live young; the platypus and echidna lay eggs.
What are the types of animals by what they eat?
Herbivores eat plants (cow, elephant, deer); carnivores eat meat (tiger, lion, eagle); omnivores eat both (humans, bears, crows); decomposers like fungi and bacteria break down dead matter.
What are the classes of vertebrates?
Vertebrates (animals with a backbone) are grouped into fish, amphibians (frogs), reptiles (snakes, lizards, crocodiles), birds and mammals.
What is the national animal of other countries?
Some national animals: India – Bengal tiger; USA – bald eagle; China – giant panda; Australia – kangaroo; UK – lion; Japan – green pheasant; South Africa – springbok.

Tigers are endangered by loss of forests, poaching for skins and body parts, and conflict with people. India's Project Tiger (1973) helped: India now has about 75% of the world's wild tigers. International Tiger Day is 29 July.

An endangered species is at high risk of dying out in the wild. Examples: tiger, snow leopard, Asian elephant, Great Indian Bustard, red panda, Ganges river dolphin. Extinct animals include the dodo and the dinosaurs.
How did the dinosaurs die out?

Most scientists agree dinosaurs died out about 66 million years ago after a huge asteroid hit near Chicxulub, Mexico, causing fires, darkness and climate change, with volcanic eruptions possibly adding to it. Birds are living descendants of dinosaurs.
What is the largest tree in the world?
The largest tree by volume is General Sherman, a giant sequoia in California. The tallest is Hyperion, a coast redwood about 116 m tall. India's Great Banyan in Kolkata is one of the widest trees.

Biodiversity is the variety of life — genes, species and ecosystems. India is one of the world's megadiverse countries, with four biodiversity hotspots: the Himalayas, the Western Ghats, Indo-Burma and Sundaland (Nicobar Islands).

Pollution is harmful material added to the environment: air pollution (smoke, vehicle exhaust, PM2.5), water pollution (sewage, chemicals), soil pollution (pesticides, plastics), noise pollution and light pollution. Reduce, reuse and recycle help.
Why is the ozone layer important?

The ozone layer, in the stratosphere about 15–35 km up, absorbs most of the Sun's harmful ultraviolet rays. CFC gases thinned it (the ozone hole over Antarctica), but the 1987 Montreal Protocol banned them and it's slowly recovering. World Ozone Day is 16 September.

Renewable energy comes from sources that don't run out: solar, wind, hydro (water), geothermal, tidal and biomass. Non-renewable sources are fossil fuels (coal, oil, natural gas) and nuclear fuel. Tamil Nadu is a leader in wind energy (Muppandal wind farm).
How many bones does a cat have?
A cat has about 230–250 bones (more than a human's 206), many in its flexible spine and tail.
How many hearts does an octopus have?
An octopus has three hearts and blue blood (because its blood uses copper-based haemocyanin). It also has eight arms and can change colour.
Flightless birds include the ostrich (the largest bird), emu, penguin, kiwi, cassowary and the extinct dodo.
Which animal is known as the ship of the desert?
The camel is called the ship of the desert: it can go days without water and its humps store fat, not water.
